newsitem.title: USA: Inktomi in Brazil search deal with Universo.
newsitem.headline: Inktomi in Brazil search deal with Universo.

text.p: Privately held Inktomi Corp said Brazil-based Universo Online (UOL) will use its Internet search technology in a search service tailored for South American and Portuguese-speakers.

The service, dubbed Radar UOL, is due to be available immediately on Monday at http://www.radaruol.com.br) and will be part of Inktomi's global search infrastructure, including Wired Ventures' HotBot in the U.S. market, OzEmail in Australia and New Zealand and NTT in Japan.
UOL is jointly owned by two of Brazil's largest media companies, Grupo Folha and Grupo Abril, Inktomi said.
UOL began operations in April 1996 and now claims some 2.8 million daily page views and more than 360,000 users.

Inktomi, which was started with financing from individuals in Florida and Texas, said in April it had raised $8 million in a first venture round from Palo Alto, Calif.-based Oak Investment Partners. (sam.perry@reuters.com, Palo Alto Bureau 415 846 5400)
